1. Case 1: Left extracranial VA dissection
A 36-year-old man with low vascular risk factors developed acute dizziness, vomiting, and gait instability after large head/neck rotation. Examination showed central cerebellar signs. Brain MRI confirmed multiple left posterior circulation infarcts, supporting a vascular etiology. CTA revealed left vertebral artery V2-V3 fenestration without a definite dissection flap; however, dedicated vessel wall imaging or DSA was not performed. Given the typical rotational injury site at V2-V3, low atherosclerotic risk, and MRI-confirmed infarcts, left extracranial vertebral artery dissection remains the leading hypothesis, more likely than fenestration-related thromboembolism. Demyelinating, peripheral vestibular, and tumor causes are effectively excluded by infarct pattern and normal CSF. Further vessel wall MRI or DSA is recommended for definitive confirmation.

Here is the reference diagnosis for this case:
1. Case 1: Acute cerebral infarction of posterior circulation associated with vertebral artery fenestration deformity
